title: Kahoot! Game-Based Digital Learning Platform: A Comprehensive Meta-Analysis https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1111/jcal.13084
author: Barton, Craig
source: Tips for Teachers (tipsforteachers.co.uk), January 15, 2025 — original paper:
summary: Barton's summary covers Ozdemir's meta-analysis of 43 experimental studies (over 3,000 students) examining the game-based quiz platform Kahoot!'s effect on academic outcomes. The synthesis finds a significant moderate positive effect on academic achievement, a very large positive effect on retention, and a large positive effect on motivation, alongside a small reduction in anxiety and a moderate improvement in attitudes toward learning. The paper attributes these gains to gamification and instant feedback, which increase active participation and engagement, and it frames Kahoot! as an effective tool for formative assessment as well as a standalone motivational device. It cautions, however, that effectiveness varies by context — subject matter, student age, and how carefully the tool is integrated into a lesson all moderate the size of the benefit — and flags technical issues (connectivity, pacing) as a practical constraint on the classroom-level results found in the underlying studies.
points: Across 43 studies and 3,000+ students, Kahoot! shows a very large positive effect on retention and a large positive effect on motivation, alongside a more moderate boost to academic achievement.
The platform's instant feedback loop is credited as a specific mechanism: it reinforces correct concepts and surfaces misconceptions in real time during formative assessment.
Effect sizes are context-dependent — subject matter, student age, and how deliberately the tool is woven into instructional goals all moderate how much Kahoot! actually helps.
Technical friction (connectivity, pacing issues) is flagged as a real-world constraint that can blunt the benefits found under controlled study conditions.
quotes: The study synthesized data from 43 experimental studies involving over 3000 students, analyzing Kahoot!'s effects on academic achievement, retention, motivation, anxiety, and attitudes toward learning.
Results indicate significant positive effects on achievement, retention, and motivation, a small negative effect on anxiety, and a moderate positive effect on attitudes.
Kahoot! has a very large positive effect on retention, suggesting students retain information better when using the platform.
Kahoot! provides instant feedback, reinforcing learning concepts and addressing misconceptions. Teachers can use this feedback loop to enhance academic outcomes.
The effectiveness of Kahoot! varies depending on the context. Teachers must consider factors such as subject matter, student age, and specific learning goals when using Kahoot!.
These results underscore the potential of Kahoot as an effective educational tool
